claim: A failed JWKS fetch logs only the exception's class name, so every failure `_fetch` detects itself (a non-200 status, a body over 1 MiB, no `keys` list, no usable signing key) comes out as the same `reason: "_JwksError"`, and the operator facing the 503s cannot tell a wrong JWKS URL from an IdP outage or from a key set Enterich cannot use.
evidence: src/enterich/auth.py:113 `raise _JwksError(f"status {response.status_code}")`, :118 `raise _JwksError("too large")`, :122 `raise _JwksError("no keys")`, :140 `raise _JwksError("no usable signing keys")`; all are caught at :103-104 `except (httpx2.HTTPError, ValueError, _JwksError) as exc: log.event("jwks", logging.WARNING, outcome="failed", reason=type(exc).__name__, keys=0)`, which drops the message. Concrete case: ENTERICH_JWKS_URL points at a path that answers 404, or the realm publishes only keys PyJWT cannot parse or that are marked `use: enc`. Each request then gets 503 with Retry-After: 30 (app.py `_mcp`), and the only diagnostic line is `{"event":"jwks","outcome":"failed","reason":"_JwksError","keys":0}`, the same line for all four causes. tests/unit/test_auth.py:370 pins `"reason": "_JwksError"` for the status case, so the lost detail is never checked.
proposal: Test: in tests/unit/test_auth.py, give the FakeJwks or MockTransport a 404 response and, separately, a JWKS whose only key is unusable (the existing `broken` RSA key), call verify_token, expect KeysUnavailable, and assert that the `jwks` line's reason tells the two apart (for example `status 404` and `no usable signing keys`). Change: in `_refresh`, log `reason=str(exc)` for `_JwksError` (its messages hold no secret and no token) and keep `type(exc).__name__` for httpx2.HTTPError and ValueError; update the expectation at test_auth.py:370.

verdict.reproduction: Raise side: src/enterich/auth.py:113 `raise _JwksError(f"status {response.status_code}")`, :118 `raise _JwksError("too large")`, :122 `raise _JwksError("no keys")`, :140 `raise _JwksError("no usable signing keys")`. Catch side: src/enterich/auth.py:103-104 `except (httpx2.HTTPError, ValueError, _JwksError) as exc: log.event("jwks", logging.WARNING, outcome="failed", reason=type(exc).__name__, keys=0)` keeps only the class name, so all four causes log the same `reason: "_JwksError"`. The message is not logged anywhere else, and the caller gets only KeysUnavailable (auth.py:84), which becomes a 503. tests/unit/test_auth.py:370 pins `"reason": "_JwksError"` for the down case. A test that asserts the reason tells a 404 apart from the `broken` RSA key case (test_auth.py:373) fails on the code as it is.
verdict.reason: I read auth.py:97-141. Each of _fetch's own checks raises _JwksError with its own message, and _refresh logs only type(exc).__name__, so the message is lost. Nothing earlier rules these inputs out: a wrong URL that answers 404, a realm whose keys are all `use: enc`, and keys PyJWT cannot parse are all real configurations. The cause also does not reach the operator any other way: verify_token raises a bare KeysUnavailable, which becomes a 503. Transport failures keep useful class names (ConnectError and so on), but the four _JwksError causes cannot be told apart. REQ-002-PRS-NF008 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:214) asks the `jwks` line only for outcome and key count, so logging the message stays within the spec. The messages carry no token or secret, so the security lens is not touched. No ADR or backlog item covers this. It is not a test-only gap: the code itself throws away the information. Pattern: none of the three fits.

claim: If building the result fails after ERPNext saved a draft, the fallback result starts a new warnings list with only the generic failure warning. The duplicate warning, worked out before the write, is lost, so neither the agent nor the draft's comment says the draft may duplicate an existing one.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:create_draft_sales_invoice runs the duplicate check before the insert (`matches = await drafts.duplicates(...)`). After `saved = await drafts.insert(...)` it sets `warnings = [drafts.duplicate_warning(matches, DRAFT_MATCH)] if matches else []` and calls `drafts.result(...)`. That calls `invoicing.tax_summary(saved)`, and `shapes.decimal` raises `ErpnextError("ERPNext's answer has a value that isn't a number.")` on a tax detail that isn't a number. The exception reaches `_attempt`. There `meter.written` is set, so `result = _written(context, op, meter.written, exc, call)` runs, and src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:_written returns `"warnings": [f"ERPNext saved the draft, but Enterich couldn't build the rest of this result ({failure...}). Read the draft to see it."]`. Nothing from the operation's own warnings carries over. `_attempt` then passes that list to `_comment`, so the comment ERPNext stores holds no duplicate match either. Concrete case: `create_draft_sales_invoice` with `allow_duplicate: true` and the same customer, posting date and items as draft SINV-0001, where ERPNext's saved answer has an `item_wise_tax_details` amount that isn't a number (the failure REQ-001-PRS-F015's Definition of Done names). The agent gets only the generic warning, never 'Possible duplicate of SINV-0001'. The draft's comment lacks the match, although REQ-001-PRS-F015's Definition of Done says a create with allow_duplicate that matches a draft leaves a comment naming the match. The same holds for returns.create (order_to_cash.py and procure_to_pay.py call `drafts.result(..., warnings)` after it), for procure_to_pay's bill-number match, and for bank_and_cash's payment match, including on update.
proposal: Test, in tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py beside test_a_written_draft_whose_result_fails_is_still_returned: seed a matching draft, monkeypatch `invoicing.tax_summary` to raise ErpnextError, and create with allow_duplicate true. Assert that one of the result's warnings starts with 'Possible duplicate of' and names the seeded draft, and that the single comment in erp.comments holds it too. Today this fails. Change: let the operation hand over the warnings it knows before the write together with the write. For example, `drafts.insert` / `drafts.save_update` take a `warnings` argument that is stored on the meter beside `written` (a `Meter.warnings` list). `_written` then returns `[*meter.warnings, <failure warning>]` in place of the failure warning alone.

verdict.reproduction:
src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:279-291: the duplicate check runs before the write (`matches = await drafts.duplicates(...)`), then `saved = await drafts.insert(context, "Sales Invoice", doc)` (which sets meter.written, src/enterich/erpnext.py:82), and only after that `warnings = [drafts.duplicate_warning(matches, DRAFT_MATCH)] if matches else []` and `return drafts.result(..., warnings)`. drafts.result calls `invoicing.tax_summary(saved)` (src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:310), and that call can raise. src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:318-326: the exception is caught, and because `meter.written` is set, `result = _written(context, op, meter.written, exc, call)` runs. src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:343-363: `_written` builds `"warnings": [f"ERPNext saved the draft, but Enterich couldn't build the rest of this result (...). Read the draft to see it."]` from scratch. src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:337-339 then passes only that list to `_comment`. What I ran: a throwaway pytest at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/lost/test_lost.py, using the repo's conftest fixtures and the `create`/`erp` helpers from tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py. It does one create, monkeypatches invoicing.tax_summary to raise ErpnextError, then creates again with allow_duplicate=True. Output: the warnings were only ["ERPNext saved the draft, but Enterich couldn't build the rest of this result (ERPNext's tax detail isn't a number). Read the draft to see it."], and the comment was "Enterich: create_draft_sales_invoice, call ....

verdict.reason: Confirmed. The duplicate match is known before the write (order_to_cash.py:279), but it only becomes a warning after the write (order_to_cash.py:288). When drafts.result then fails (drafts.py:310), _attempt (tools/__init__.py:326) falls back to _written (tools/__init__.py:343), which starts a fresh warnings list with only the generic failure. The agent never learns the draft may duplicate an existing one, and the draft's comment doesn't say so either. REQ-001-PRS-F015 requires the comment to carry the result's warnings, and its Definition of Done says a create with allow_duplicate that matches a draft leaves a comment naming the match. No earlier check rules this input out. The existing test test_a_written_draft_whose_result_fails_is_still_returned uses no duplicate, so it doesn't cover this path. The fix stays within the specs and ADRs: a warning known before the write is kept with the write (for example on the Meter) and _written puts it ahead of the failure warning. A failing test in tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py shows the gap. The other paths the finding names (returns, procure_to_pay's bill-number match, bank_and_cash's match) follow the same mechanism; I didn't run them. None of the listed patterns fits.

claim: The duplicate check reads only the first 1,000 account rows of the day's drafts and says nothing when it hits that cap, so a repeated create whose earlier draft falls past the cap goes through with no refusal and no warning.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:_journal_duplicates calls `context.erpnext.get_list("Journal Entry", fields=("name", "accounts.account", ...), filters=[company, docstatus 0, posting_date], order_by="name asc", start=0, page_length=drafts.MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS)` with MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS = 1000 (src/enterich/tools/drafts.py). The list returns one row per account row, ordered by name, and nothing checks whether `len(found) == MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS`. Example state: the company already has 1,000 or more draft journal-entry account rows on 2026-11-19 (say 500 two-row drafts). The agent creates ACC-JV-2026-00601, loses the answer and sends the same create again. Naming-series names sort ascending, so the newest draft's rows come last and are the ones past the 1,000-row page. Its rows are missing, or only partly there, so `_same_rows(wanted, stored)` is False, `matches` is [], and `create_draft_journal_entry` inserts a second draft with no `allow_duplicate` refusal and no 'Possible duplicate' warning. The spec's ERPNext calls table for REQ-006 says the duplicate check is 'in one call' and names no cap, unlike the Fiscal Year read, where it says 'at most 1,000'. So neither the agent nor the reviewer learns that the check was incomplete.
proposal: Test: give the fake ERPNext a Journal Entry draft list on the posting date that fills MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS rows, with the matching draft's rows at the end past the page, then call create_draft_journal_entry with the same rows. Today it inserts silently; it should refuse naming the match, or at least warn. Change: when `len(found) == drafts.MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS`, either read the next page (start += page_length) until a short page comes back, or put a warning in the result (and so in the draft's comment) saying the duplicate check couldn't read every draft on the date. The same applies to the shared drafts.duplicates for invoices.

verdict.reproduction: Side one, the capped read: src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:516-532 `found = await context.erpnext.get_list("Journal Entry", fields=("name", "accounts.account", ...), filters=[company, docstatus 0, posting_date], order_by="name asc", start=0, page_length=drafts.MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS)` with src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:26 `MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS = 1000`. Lines 533-541 group the rows by name and compare them, and nothing checks `len(found) == MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS`. Side two, what gets reported: record_to_report.py:583-591 `matches = await _journal_duplicates(...)`, `if matches and not inputs.allow_duplicate: raise drafts.refuse_duplicates(...)`, `warnings = [drafts.duplicate_warning(...)] if matches else []`. When the earlier draft falls past the cap, the create gets neither a refusal nor a warning. The spec (docs/specs/req-006-record-to-report.md:209) says the duplicate check runs "in one call" and names no cap; REQ-001-URS-F007 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:152) says a duplicate "SHALL NOT go through unnoticed". What I ran: a throwaway test at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/cap/test_cap.py against tests/fakes and the integration MCP client (PYTHONPATH=. uv run pytest -p tests.conftest -p tests.integration.conftest). It seeds 500 two-row Journal Entry drafts on TODAY (1,000 account rows), creates a draft with rows Rent debit 800 / Bank credit 800 (ACC-JV-2026-00601, warnings []), then sends the same create again. The second call returned no error and inserted ACC-JV-2026-00602.
verdict.reason: Confirmed. I read _journal_duplicates (src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:511-541) and the shared drafts.duplicates (src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:69-89). Both read one page of MAX_DUPLICATE_ROWS=1000 child rows, ordered by name ascending, and never notice when the page is full. Naming-series names rise over time, so the newest draft, the one a lost-answer retry repeats, is the first to fall past the cap. The retry then goes through with no refusal and no 'Possible duplicate' warning, so neither the agent nor the reviewer learns the check was cut short; running the fake confirmed this. Nothing rules the state out. The limit of drafts per hour caps only the agent's own creates (config allows up to 1,000 per hour), and the check counts people's drafts too (REQ-001-PRS-F005). The backlog doesn't list this, and no ADR chose it: REQ-001's accepted limitations (req-001-core.md:739) name only two creates at the same instant. It isn't a fix within the current specs, though. The REQ-006 calls table says the check runs 'in one call', so reading further pages would change the spec. A warning that the check couldn't read every draft has no text in the specs, which define each warning. And the same gap sits in the shared helper used by the invoice, return and bank-and-cash creates (procure_to_pay.py:325, returns.py:204, bank_and_cash.py:425, drafts.py:82), so closing it for all of them means amending REQ-001-PRS-F005 or the area specs' calls tables first. That makes this a proposal. None of the listed patterns fits.

claim: If an invoice or party in a payment entry's `references` is given in a different letter case than ERPNext stores it, the payment is refused with a false cause: the invoice "doesn't exist", or it is "another party's". ERPNext's own query does find the invoice, so the agent is told the wrong thing and may book the payment without the reference, as an unallocated advance.
evidence: The invoices are fetched with `filters=[["company", "=", ...], ["name", "in", names]]`. ERPNext matches names regardless of case, as src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:get_item notes ("ERPNext finds names case-insensitively; the link carries the stored one") and as drafts._folded allows for. But the rows are then looked up by exact case: `found = {str(row.get("name")): row for row in rows}` and `row = found.get(name)`, followed by `if row is None: raise unknown_name("references", what, name)`. Example: create_draft_payment_entry with party "Acme" and references [{reference_name: "acc-sinv-2026-00001", ...}], where ERPNext stores ACC-SINV-2026-00001 for Acme. get_list returns the row named "ACC-SINV-2026-00001", `found.get("acc-sinv-2026-00001")` is None, and the agent is told "references: the sales invoice 'acc-sinv-2026-00001' doesn't exist, or the agent user isn't permitted to read it." The party check has the same flaw: `if row.get(side.party_field) != party` compares exact text, so party "acme" (which ERPNext accepts as the link to Acme) gets "ACC-SINV-2026-00001 is Acme's invoice, not acme's." The tool description tells the agent that a payment without references is booked as an advance, so the agent may drop the reference it was falsely told is missing.
proposal: Test: in tests for create_draft_payment_entry, make the fake's get_list return the submitted, open invoice under its stored upper-case name and party, call the tool with the reference_name lowercased, and assert that the payment is not refused as unknown (it saves, with the reference sent). Do the same with the party lowercased and assert that it is not refused as another party's invoice. Change: key `found` by `str(row.get("name")).casefold()` and look it up with `name.casefold()`; compare the party with `drafts._folded(row.get(side.party_field)) != drafts._folded(party)`, or with a shared helper so the case rule is written in one place. Also send the stored name (`row["name"]`) in `_allocations`.

verdict.reproduction: src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:370 sends the query `filters=[["company", "=", context.settings.company], ["name", "in", names]]`, and ERPNext's MariaDB (utf8mb4_unicode_ci) matches it without regard to letter case, so a reference given as "acc-sinv-2026-00001" gets back the row stored as "ACC-SINV-2026-00001". The lookup after that uses exact text: bank_and_cash.py:375 `found = {str(row.get("name")): row for row in rows}` and :379-381 `row = found.get(name)` / `if row is None: raise unknown_name("references", what, name)`. So the agent is told that the invoice doesn't exist, or that it may not read it, when the invoice is there. The party check has the same flaw: bank_and_cash.py:385 `if row.get(side.party_field) != party:` refuses party "acme" with "... is Acme's invoice, not acme's." ERPNext would accept "acme" as the link to Acme. The codebase already handles case elsewhere: src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:241-242 and :257-258 (`_folded`, "ERPNext saves a link in the stored name's case") and src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:95 ("ERPNext finds names case-insensitively; the link carries the stored one"). Nothing run: the fake tests/fakes/erpnext.py:1142-1143 matches `in` exactly (`actual in value`), so it can't show this as it is. The test has to make the fake's get_list return the stored upper-case row for a lower-case reference_name, or the lower-case party.
verdict.reason: I read _check_references (src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:343-402) and its two callers (:494 create, :548 update). Nothing before the check puts reference_name or party into the stored case: Allocation.reference_name is a plain Name (:207), and create passes inputs.party straight through. The query matches names without regard to case, but the result is looked up and compared by exact text. Elsewhere the code allows for ERPNext's case-insensitive names (drafts._folded at drafts.py:257, master_data.py:95), and no spec or ADR asks for exact case here. So a real invoice gets a false cause ("doesn't exist" or "another party's"). The agent loses the real state of the invoice and, as the tool's description suggests, may book the payment as an unallocated advance. A test can show the code wrong if it makes the fake return the stored-case row. The fix: compare with casefold, through drafts._folded or a shared helper, and send the stored row["name"] in _allocations. None of the listed patterns fits.

claim: The ageing ranges are written in three places: the boundaries sent to ERPNext, the number of buckets Enterich reads back, and the bucket ranges both report descriptions tell the agent. Change the boundaries in one place and the other two stay as they were.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:aged_report sends `"range": "30, 60, 90, 120",`. src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:AGEING is `tuple(f"range{i}" for i in range(6))  # range0: not yet due; then ERPNext's 30, 60, 90, 120`. src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py report_accounts_receivable description and src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py report_accounts_payable description both say "then `range1` to `range5` for 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-120 and over 120 days". Example: adding a boundary ("30, 60, 90, 120, 180") makes ERPNext return range6, which AGEING drops, while both descriptions still give the old ranges.
proposal: Define one constant, e.g. `AGEING_DAYS = (30, 60, 90, 120)`. Build the filter from it with `", ".join(map(str, AGEING_DAYS))`, set `AGEING = tuple(f"range{i}" for i in range(len(AGEING_DAYS) + 2))`, and generate the description sentence (one shared `AGEING_NOTE` in invoicing) from it for both reports. Test: one unit test asserting that the filter's boundary count, len(AGEING) and the description text all follow the one constant.

verdict.reproduction: src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:288 `"range": "30, 60, 90, 120",` (the boundaries sent to ERPNext). src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:43 `AGEING = tuple(f"range{i}" for i in range(6))  # range0: not yet due; then ERPNext's 30, 60, 90, 120` (bucket count read back at :298 `"ageing": {r: row.get(r) for r in AGEING}`). src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:414-415 and src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:552-553 both say "`range0` not yet due, then `range1` to `range5` for 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-120 and over 120 days". Nothing derives one from another: a change of the filter to "30, 60, 90, 120, 180" would make ERPNext return range6, which AGEING's hard-coded 6 drops, and both descriptions would still list the old ranges. Not run; it follows from reading the code.
verdict.reason: I confirmed the finding. All three places describe the same ageing-bucket rule, and none of them is derived from another, so a change to the boundaries in invoicing.py:288 would leave AGEING (:43) and the two tool descriptions (order_to_cash.py:415, procure_to_pay.py:552-553) out of date. The values are not equal by chance or meant to differ: the comment at :43 ties AGEING to the boundaries. It is not the docs lens's case either, because the descriptions are code the agent receives. The ranges are fixed in the specs (docs/specs/req-004-order-to-cash.md:168,199; docs/specs/req-005-procure-to-pay.md:189,222). So today all three places behave the same, no failing test can show the gap, and changing the ranges would need a spec change first. That makes it a restructure: a proposal, not a fix. The backlog does not list it.

claim: The General Ledger's day limit is a constant in the validator, but the tool description the agent reads has the number typed in, so changing MAX_LEDGER_DAYS leaves the agent with the old limit.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:MAX_LEDGER_DAYS is `MAX_LEDGER_DAYS = 366`, and ReportGeneralLedger._rules uses it (`if (self.to_date - self.from_date).days + 1 > MAX_LEDGER_DAYS`). The Operation's description says the literal "from `from_date` to `to_date` (at most 366 days)". Set MAX_LEDGER_DAYS = 92 and the description still promises 366 days; the agent's calls are then refused for a limit it was never told.
proposal: Build the description with an f-string: `f"... (at most {MAX_LEDGER_DAYS} days) ..."`. Test: assert that str(MAX_LEDGER_DAYS) appears in the report_general_ledger operation's description.

verdict.reproduction: src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:102 `MAX_LEDGER_DAYS = 366`, used at :188 `if (self.to_date - self.from_date).days + 1 > MAX_LEDGER_DAYS:` and in the refusal at :190 `f"from_date to to_date must span at most {MAX_LEDGER_DAYS} days, both included"`. The agent-facing description at src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:698 types the number in: `"The assigned company's General Ledger from `from_date` to `to_date` (at most 366 "`. If MAX_LEDGER_DAYS is changed (e.g. to 92), the validator and refusal follow but the description still says 366. tests/snapshots/tools.json:2256 snapshots only the description, so it keeps passing when only the constant changes.
verdict.reason: Both places are one rule (REQ-006-RTR-F003, docs/specs/req-006-record-to-report.md:73: at most 366 days). The constant drives the check and the refusal (record_to_report.py:102, :188, :190), but the description the agent reads has the literal 366 (:698). Changing the constant would leave the description behind, and the description snapshot (tests/snapshots/tools.json:2256) would not catch that because the description would not change. Today both say 366, so no test fails on the current code. Closing it is a restructure: build the description from MAX_LEDGER_DAYS, plus an optional guard test. So the class is proposal, not fix. None of the listed patterns fit.

claim: The result size limit is a constant in shapes.to_text, but the two messages that tell the agent what the limit is have the number typed in, so changing the limit leaves both messages wrong.
evidence: src/enterich/shapes.py:MAX_RESULT_CHARS is `MAX_RESULT_CHARS = 100_000`, and to_text uses it (`return text if len(text) < MAX_RESULT_CHARS else None`). src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:_attempt refuses with the literal "The result would exceed 100,000 characters: narrow a list or report ...". src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:_without warns with the literal "...: with them it would exceed 100,000 characters. Read the draft to see them." Lower MAX_RESULT_CHARS to 50_000 and both texts still say 100,000.
proposal: Import MAX_RESULT_CHARS into tools/__init__.py and write both messages as `f"... exceed {MAX_RESULT_CHARS:,} characters ..."`. Test: monkeypatch shapes.MAX_RESULT_CHARS to a small value, run a read whose result is larger, and assert the refusal names the patched value.

verdict.reproduction: The limit: src/enterich/shapes.py:20 `MAX_RESULT_CHARS = 100_000`, applied at src/enterich/shapes.py:230 `return text if len(text) < MAX_RESULT_CHARS else None`. The read refusal states it as a literal: src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:331 `"The result would exceed 100,000 characters: narrow a list or report (a search, "`. The warning for a draft result without its tables states it as a literal: src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:389-390 `f"This result leaves out the draft's {', '.join(left_out)}: with them it would exceed " "100,000 characters. Read the draft to see them."`. The same file already builds the timeout message from its constant (`f"The operation took longer than {OPERATION_TIMEOUT:g} seconds."`, src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:321), so the limit message is the place that doesn't follow that pattern. tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:741 already patches `shapes.MAX_RESULT_CHARS` to 2_000. Under that patch the code leaves out the tables at 2,000 characters, but the warning still says 100,000. That test only checks `"items" in left_out`, so it doesn't notice. Nothing was run; reading the code is enough.
verdict.reason: Both messages state the limit that shapes.MAX_RESULT_CHARS enforces (src/enterich/shapes.py:20,230), and both have the number typed in (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:331, :390). A maintainer who changes the constant would leave both texts wrong. The values are one rule, not equal by chance: each message tells the agent the limit it just ran into. No ADR or backlog entry chooses to keep them literal, and the same file builds OPERATION_TIMEOUT's message from its constant (line 321). Today the deployed behaviour is right in both places: the constant is 100_000, as REQ-001-PRS-NF003 sets it (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:611). Changing the limit would also change the spec.
